Waste sorting can be difficult in everyday life, especially when an item does not clearly belong in one bin.

In Denmark, municipalities generally use waste fractions such as food waste, paper, cardboard, metal, glass, plastic, food and beverage cartons, textile waste, hazardous waste and residual waste. Local schemes can still vary.

Waste Guide Denmark is an independent sorting guide and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or operated by any government authority, municipality or public waste company. The app is made to help you find a quick and useful answer, but official and local rules should always be checked with the municipality or relevant official sources.

In Waste Guide Denmark you can search for a waste item and see which waste fraction it typically belongs to.

The search function uses a local database in the app, so the most important sorting information is available quickly.

The app is a practical sorting guide. If you are unsure about local rules, large items or special drop-off points, always check your municipality’s own instructions.

Waste Guide Denmark is developed by Simple Web, owned by Oliver Kronholm Thomsen.

Besides Waste Guide Denmark, I also run simplecode.dk, whenrocketsfly.com and elis-icebreakers.com.

If you have questions, feedback or suggestions for the app, you are welcome to contact me at info@simplecode.dk.

Waste Guide Denmark is made to provide simple and quick help with waste sorting. The app does not ask for your name, address or e-mail address to use the normal search function.

The search function uses a local waste database stored in the app. This means the waste search itself does not need to fetch sorting data from external databases.

The app uses Google AdMob for ads. AdMob may process technical information such as device information, app version, ad data and general usage statistics. The information is used to show and measure ads and to maintain and improve app operation.

Waste Guide Denmark does not sell your personal information. Information is processed only where necessary for app operation, advertising or where required by law.

If you have questions about this privacy policy, you can write to info@simplecode.dk.

We reserve the right to update this privacy policy. Changes will be made available in the app.

Waste Guide Denmark is an independent guidance app. The app is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by or operated by any government authority, municipality or public waste company.

The information in the app is provided for practical guidance and general information only. We try to keep the information correct and useful, but cannot guarantee that all information is always complete, updated or valid in every municipality.

Waste schemes, bins, recycling centres, contact details and local rules may vary and change. If in doubt, especially about hazardous waste, large items or special drop-off requirements, always check the rules with your municipality, recycling centre or relevant official sources.

Official sources and verification:
borger.dk: https://www.borger.dk/miljoe-og-energi/Affald-og-genbrug
Danish Environmental Protection Agency: https://mst.dk
Municipality-specific information should be verified on the official website of the relevant municipality, which may be linked in the app.

Use of the app is at your own responsibility. Simple Web is not liable for errors, omissions or decisions made based on the app’s content.
Search for waste and see which waste fraction it belongs to.
What if my municipality does not have a bin for the shown waste fraction?
Check your municipality’s instructions. Many waste types can be taken to a recycling centre or handled through special collection schemes. Hazardous waste should never be thrown in residual waste.
What if the app cannot find my waste item?
Try a more common word or another spelling. You can also check mit-affald.dk, your municipality’s website or ask at your local recycling centre.
Why was my waste bin not emptied?
Contact your municipality or local waste company. They can provide information about collection days, reports and local rules.
Does the app use my phone camera?
No. The current version does not use the camera. You can search for waste directly in the search field.
Can I help add waste items?
Yes. If you find a missing or incorrect item, please contact me at info@simplecode.dk so the database can be improved.
Why do the pictograms not always look like the ones on my bins?
Pictograms can vary between municipalities, bins and packaging. The app uses pictograms as a visual aid, but you should follow the text and your municipality’s local instructions if they differ.
Can the app be used in all municipalities?
The app can be used as a general sorting guide throughout Denmark. Local differences may exist, so your municipality’s own rules always come first.
How should I handle large items or furniture?

Large items and furniture should usually be taken to a recycling centre or handled as bulky waste. Some municipalities offer collection days or booking. Check the bulky waste rules in your municipality.
Which liquid waste can I pour into the sink?

As a rule, only small amounts of ordinary water-based liquids should go into the sink. Avoid fat, oil, paint, solvents, chemicals, candle wax, coffee grounds and anything that can harm drains, treatment plants or the environment.
Where can I find updated waste sorting rules for my municipality?

You can find updated information on your municipality’s website, from your local waste company or at borger.dk. You can also use mit-affald.dk to find links and contact details for many municipalities.
